When empty, OpenRouter\n431\t# uses \"google/gemini-3-flash-preview\" and Nous uses \"gemini-3-flash\".\n432\t# Other providers pick a sensible default automatically.\n433\t#\n434\t# auxiliary:\n435\t#   # Image analysis: vision_analyze tool + browser screenshots\n436\t#   vision:\n437\t#     provider: \"auto\"\n438\t#     model: \"\"              # e.g. \"google/gemini-2.5-flash\", \"openai/gpt-4o\"\n439\t#     timeout: 30            # LLM API call timeout (seconds)\n440\t#     download_timeout: 30   # Image HTTP download timeout (seconds)\n441\t#                            # Increase for slow connections or self-hosted image servers\n442\t#\n443\t#   # Web page scraping / summarization + browser page text extraction\n444\t#   web_extract:\n445\t#     provider: \"auto\"\n446\t#     model: \"\"\n447\t#\n448\t#   # Session search — summarizes matching past sessions\n449\t#   session_search:\n450\t#     provider: \"auto\"\n451\t#     model: \"\"\n452\t#     timeout: 30\n453\t#     max_concurrency: 3    # Limit parallel summaries to reduce request-burst 429s\n454\t#     extra_body: {}        # Provider-specific OpenAI-compatible request fields\n455\t#                           # Example for providers that support request-body\n456\t#                           # reasoning controls:\n457\t#                           # extra_body:\n458\t#                           #   enable_thinking: false\n459\t\n460\t# =============================================================================\n461\t# Persistent Memory\n462\t# =============================================================================\n463\t# Bounded curated memory injected into the system prompt every session.\n464\t# Two stores: MEMORY.md (agent's notes) and USER.md (user profile).\n465\t# Character limits keep the memory small and focused. The agent manages\n466\t# pruning -- when at the limit, it must consolidate or replace entries.\n467\t# Disabled by default in batch_runner.\n468\t#\n469\tmemory:\n470\t  # Agent's personal notes: environment facts, conventions, things learned\n471\t  memory_enabled: true\n472\t  \n473\t  # User profile: preferences, communication style, expectations\n474\t  user_profile_enabled: true\n475\t  \n476\t  # Character limits (~2.75 chars per token, model-independent)\n477\t  memory_char_limit: 2200   # ~800 tokens\n478\t  user_char_limit: 1375     # ~500 tokens\n479\t\n480\t  # Periodic memory nudge: remind the agent to consider saving memories\n481\t  # every N user turns. Set to 0 to disable. Only active when memory is enabled.\n482\t  nudge_interval: 10        # Nudge every 10 user turns (0 = disabled)\n483\t\n484\t  # Memory flush: give the agent one turn to save memories before context is\n485\t  # lost (compression, /new, /reset, exit). Set to 0 to disable.\n486\t  # For exit/reset, only fires if the session had at least this many user turns.\n487\t  flush_min_turns: 6        # Min user turns to trigger flush on exit/reset (0 = disabled)\n488\t\n489\t# =============================================================================\n490\t# Session Reset Policy (Messaging Platforms)\n491\t# =============================================================================\n492\t# Controls when messaging sessions (Telegram, Discord, WhatsApp, Slack) are\n493\t# automatically cleared. Without resets, conversation context grows indefinitely\n494\t# which increases API costs with every message.\n495\t#\n496\t# When a reset triggers, the agent first saves important information to its\n497\t# persistent memory — but the conversation context is wiped. The agent starts\n498\t# fresh but retains learned facts via its memory system.\n499\t#\n500\t# Users can always manually reset with /reset or /new in chat.\n501\t#\n502\t# Modes:\n503\t#   \"both\"  - Reset on EITHER inactivity timeout or daily boundary (recommended)\n504\t#   \"idle\"  - Reset only after N minutes of inactivity\n505\t#   \"daily\" - Reset only at a fixed hour each day\n506\t#   \"none\"  - Never auto-reset; context lives until /reset or compression kicks in\n507\t#\n508\t# When a reset triggers, the agent gets one turn to save important memories and\n509\t# skills before the context is wiped. Tracks actual token usage from API responses (not estimates)\n# 2. When prompt_tokens >= threshold% of model's context_length, triggers compression\n# 3. Protects first 3 turns (system prompt, initial request, first response)\n# 4. Protects last N turns (default 20 messages = ~10 full turns of recent context)\n# 5. Summarizes middle turns using a fast/cheap model\n# 6. Inserts summary as a user message, continues conversation seamlessly\n#\n# Post-compression tail budget is target_ratio × threshold × context_length:\n#   200K context, threshold 0.50, ratio 0.20 → 20K tokens of recent tail preserved\n#   1M   context, threshold 0.50, ratio 0.20 → 100K tokens of recent tail preserved\n#\ncompression:\n  # Enable automatic context compression (default: true)\n  # Set to false if you prefer to manage context manually or want errors on overflow\n  enabled: true\n  \n  # Trigger compression at this % of model's context limit (default: 0.50 = 50%)\n  # Lower values = more aggressive compression, higher values = compress later\n  threshold: 0.50\n  \n  # Fraction of the threshold to preserve as recent tail (default: 0.20 = 20%)\n  # e.g. 20% of 50% threshold = 10% of total context kept as recent messages.\n  # Summary output is separately capped at 12K tokens (Gemini output limit).\n  # Range: 0.10 - 0.80\n  target_ratio: 0.20\n\n  # Number of most-recent messages to always preserve (default: 20 ≈ 10 full turns)\n  # Higher values keep more recent conversation intact at the cost of more aggressive\n  # compression of older turns.\n  protect_last_n: 20\n\n  # Number of non-system messages to protect at the head of the transcript, in\n  # ADDITION to the system prompt (which is always implicitly protected).\n  # Head messages are NEVER summarized — they survive every compression\n  # indefinitely. This gives stable early context for short/medium sessions,\n  # but in long-running sessions that rely on rolling compaction the pinned\n  # opening turns may not match how you want the session framed over time.\n  # Set to 0 to preserve ONLY the system prompt (plus the rolling summary\n  # and recent tail) — the cleanest configuration for long-running sessions.\n  # Default 3 preserves the system prompt plus the first three non-system\n  # head messages, matching the pre-feature behaviour.\n  protect_first_n: 3\n\n  # To pin a specific model/provider for compression summaries, use the\n  # auxiliary section below (auxiliary.compression.provider / model).\n\n# =============================================================================\n# Anthropic prompt caching TTL\n# =============================================================================\n# When prompt caching is active (Claude via OpenRouter or native Anthropic),\n# Anthropic supports two TTL tiers for cached prefixes: \"5m\" (default) and\n# \"1h\". Other values are ignored and \"5m\" is used.\n#\nprompt_caching:\n  cache_ttl: \"5m\" # use \"1h\" for long sessions with pauses between turns\n\n# =============================================================================\n# Auxiliary Models (Advanced — Experimental)\n# =============================================================================\n# Hermes uses lightweight \"auxiliary\" models for side tasks: image analysis,\n# browser screenshot analysis, web page summarization, and context compression.\n#\n# By default these use Gemini Flash via OpenRouter or Nous Portal and are\n# auto-detected from your credentials.
